core.text: Three irregular verbs build their imperfect a little differently: **the imperfect of the irregular verbs (eram = I was, poteram = I could, ibam = I was going)**. *esse*: *eram, erās, erat, erāmus, erātis, erant* — the stem is *era-*, the endings the usual ones. *posse* adds *pot-* in front: *poteram, poterās, poterat, poterāmus, poterātis, poterant*. *īre* uses its stem *ī-* with *-ba-* and no *e*: *ībam, ībās, ībat, ībāmus, ībātis, ībant*. The rest — *volō, nōlō, mālō, ferō* — are regular here: *volēbat, ferēbat*. Latin name: imperfectum verbōrum anomalōrum.
*Was* and *were* are the English imperfect of *be*: *he was a boy*. *Could* is the past of *can*; *was going* the past of *goes*.
eram / poteram with the -m, -s, -t endings; ībam like a 1st-conjugation imperfect; the other irregulars are regular (-ēbat).

invented.en: The boys used to go to school in the morning.

core.text: *est* — he is; *erat* — he was. *potest* — he can; *poterat* — he could. *it* — he goes; *ībat* — he was going. The present shifts its stem (*su- / es-*, *e- / ī-*); the imperfect settles on one stem (*era-*, *ī-*) and adds the past endings. If you see *era-* or *-ba-*, you are in the past.

more.text: *eram* also builds the pluperfect (the 'had done' tense): *amāverat* is *amāv-* + *erat*. So *era-* inside a longer verb means *had*. Compounds of *esse* follow *eram* — *aberat* (was away), *aderant* (were present) — and compounds of *īre* follow *ībam*: *redībat* (was going back), *exībant*.

Your notes: *su / es* uses the special stem *era-* with regular endings (*eram, erās, erat, erāmus, erātis, erant*); *possum* and all other compounds of *esse* add a prefix to the same stem (*pot-era-m*); *e / i* uses the stem *i* and the marker without its *e* (*ībam, ībās, ībat*); the other irregular verbs are regular in the imperfect, *volō* keeping the stem *vol-* (*volēbat, mālēbāmus, ferēbātur, nōlēbam*).

Ørberg (chapter XIX): *esse: eram, erāmus, erās, erātis, erat, erant*; *ante trēs hōrās nox erat*; *Iūlius tam improbus erat quam Mārcus nunc est*. A&G §170, §198, §203 give the full tables; *ferō* has *ferēbam*, and *fīō* (become) *fīēbam*.
